name: contact-form
title: Contact Form
description: A contact form whose messages land as rows in your own Supabase table — validated on the server, working without JavaScript, and with no secret to keep.

env.description: Your Supabase project's URL, e.g. https://abcdefghijklmnop.supabase.co. Setting it opens that one host to your App's outbound calls. Leave it blank to deploy first: the form then answers that it has no database yet.
env.where_to_find: Supabase → your project → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL. The Connect button at the top of the project shows it too.

env.description: The key the Function writes with. With the policy in schema.sql it can insert a row and cannot read one back.
env.where_to_find: Supabase → your project → Project Settings → API Keys → Publishable key. It starts with sb_publishable_. It is not marked secret because Supabase designs it to be public: what limits it is the insert-only policy in schema.sql, not keeping it hidden. Never put the secret key (sb_secret_) here. It skips every policy and can read and delete every row.

post_deploy:
Your contact form is live at {{url}}

If you left the two Supabase values blank, the form has no database yet, and a
message sent now is answered with a note saying so. To make it keep messages, in
this order:
  1. Create a project at https://supabase.com/dashboard.
  2. Open its SQL Editor, paste in schema.sql from this project, and run it. That
     creates the enquiries table and a policy that lets the publishable key
     insert rows and nothing else.
  3. Set the project URL (Project Settings → Data API). This also opens that one
     host to your App's outbound calls:
       wawesome env set SUPABASE_URL https://<project-ref>.supabase.co
  4. Set the publishable key (Project Settings → API Keys). It is not a secret,
     because the policy is what limits it, so no --secret:
       wawesome env set SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY sb_publishable_...
  5. Send a message from {{url}}, then open Table Editor → enquiries in Supabase.
     The row is there.

Then:
  - The words and fields are in src/page.ts; the rules are in src/enquiry.ts.
  - Watch submissions, and any refusal from Supabase, as they happen:
      wawesome logs --follow
  - Spam protection and rate limiting are yours to add. The README says what the
    policy does and does not protect.
